name: Y2K aesthetic

card.summary: A revival style drawn from late-1990s and early-2000s fashion, makeup and tech design, used to build a playful, futuristic look through metallics, low-rise cuts and glossy accessories.

quick.overview:
The Y2K aesthetic is an internet-born style based on products, fashion and design of the late 1990s and early 2000s. As a personal look it covers clothing, makeup and accessories that evoke that era, giving people a distinctive, recognisable style to dress in.

Its signature elements include PVC and metallic fabrics, futuristic sunglasses, tracksuits, platform shoes, bright colour palettes and glossy finishes. It revived strongly in the 2020s and spread via social media and music scenes such as K-pop.
quick.how: People assemble the look from period pieces or new items: low-rise trousers, velour tracksuits, baby-tee tops, trucker hats, butterfly clips, metallic or glittery makeup and wraparound sunglasses, often paired with clear or colourful tech accessories.
quick.risks: Clothing risks are minimal. Some period trends, such as very low-rise cuts, are not suited to every body or comfort preference.

lead: The Y2K aesthetic is an internet aesthetic based on products, styles and fashion of the late 1990s and early 2000s; the name comes from the abbreviation for the year 2000 [1]. In appearance terms it gives people a ready-made, coherent style to dress and make up in [1][2].

Fashion elements include PVC clothing, futuristic sunglasses, tracksuits, platform shoes and wearable technology, with animal prints and psychedelic patterns carried over from the 1990s [1]. Colour palettes feature lime, orange and hot pink with white and chrome [1]. Early-2000s Y2K fashion also used metallic fabrics, mesh tops, straps, buckles and wraparound sunglasses, with bronze-flecked metallic makeup [2].

The term became widely used in the 2020s, and scholar Xiaochun Yang links the revival to the COVID-19 pandemic and recession [1]. The style is prominent in K-pop and J-pop, for example groups such as Aespa and XG [1].

angle.text: People wear Y2K clothing, makeup and accessories to present a distinctive, playful look. It is a styling choice made directly through what is worn.

paras: Low-rise jeans were popular from about 2001, and Juicy Couture velour tracksuits and Von Dutch trucker hats were sought after; butterfly clips and crimped hair were common among teen girls [2]. Makeup used bronze specks for metallic shine, and glittery looks faded by 2004 [2].

Computers and consoles often had clear or translucent coloured casings, and digital cameras and flip phones are associated with the look [1]. Graphic design used gradients, chunky rounded fonts and glossy or metallic effects [1].

The term gained mainstream use in the 2020s and broadened to mean 2000s fashion generally; the original retrofuturist style is sometimes called Cybercore [1]. Outfits circulate under the Y2K hashtag on Xiaohongshu, celebrities have worn the style in magazines, and Japan's Y3K trend has been influenced by K-pop groups [1].
